entry.title: BIP 110: update status to closed
entry.summary:
The activation of BIP-110 occurred at the designated block height as outlined in the specification without the need for additional adoption criteria such as the "2.5%" previously mentioned. The Bitcoin Whitepaper underscores the protocol's security, stating that as long as honest nodes possess the majority of CPU power, they can create the longest blockchain and thus stay ahead of potential attackers. This assertion supports the decentralized nature of mining, where numerous nodes contribute independently to the network's robustness.
Contrary to concerns about the influence of specific nodes like "Roughnecks," it is crucial to acknowledge that their decisions do not reflect or impact the collective node population within the Bitcoin network. Currently, around 18,000 fully validating nodes operate without rejecting the implementation of the BIP-110 soft-fork, also known as RDTS. These nodes maintain the autonomy to disconnect and reconnect with the network freely, a flexibility that aligns with the principles described in the Bitcoin Whitepaper.
I recently broadcast a transaction from one of the active nodes to demonstrate that the operation adheres to established network rules and does not involve alternative cryptocurrencies. This act reinforces my stance that there is no basis for the confiscation of bitcoins as purported by some factions within the community.
